column4: Key details have user_token input but limits and purchase metadata do not establish caller ownership or membership authorization.
Hotel rate-plan listing requires an API key and provides no affirmative unrestricted-access evidence.
Account-number account_id is inferred without a verified caller-account relation or personal-versus-tenant distinction.
Transfer approval exposes account and approval metadata but no required role or verified ownership lookup.
Bank account update has entity_id but no supplied caller identity mapping or verified tenant binding.
Authorization listing can filter by user or org but only wrapper fields are available to establish access policy.
Authorization update has both orgID and userID with opaque permissions and no verified choice of authorization subject.
Bucket orgID, owners and members indicate multiple access relationships without a verified lookup or specified policy.
Removing a bucket member has user path context but only error-response columns and unknown security.
Key-value mutation has authentication alternatives but no supplied ownership, tenant or role requirement.
Brokerage order modification is account-scoped but returned order fields do not establish caller-account authorization.
Channel analytics posts expose facilitator and moderator metadata without defining the caller's required role or object access.
Account managing_account is an inferred relationship with no verified caller mapping for update authorization.
Contact consuming_account and managing_account are competing account relationships with unspecified authorization semantics.
Organization category listing has only a categories wrapper, insufficient for a verified tenant lookup.
Organization discounts require READ:PRODUCT but discount fields lack a verified organization-to-caller binding.
Discount update uses WRITE:PRODUCT permission, not a caller role, and supplies no tenant lookup relation.
Import status has organization path context but no organization field in the inferred status record.
Products visible in POS are not necessarily unrestricted API resources; organization authorization is unspecified.
Similar-artist lookup uses CustomAuthentication and userId filtering without a specific object authorization rule.
Device UserId and LastUserId are ambiguous inferred device metadata, not a verified ownership lookup.
Custom-field retrieval has unknown security and no affirmative unrestricted-access or caller-policy evidence.
Adding customers to a category exposes customer data but no caller role or verified account ownership relationship.
Publicly-accessible tag conflicts with unresolved checkout and tenant object context; available-time fields cannot establish unrestricted authorization.
Publicly-accessible tag does not prove arbitrary callers may change delivery state for an order; no object authorization evidence is supplied.
Client-scope roles are objects being changed, not a demonstrated caller role; realm-to-caller authorization is unresolved.
Payment-session customer and merchant data are flattened and security is unknown, leaving ownership binding ambiguous.
User-list isAdmin filter is not an administrator requirement; auth-key security alone does not select a supported policy.
Appointment CreatedBy is provenance alongside Staff and LinkedGuest, not a verified owner-only access relationship.
Analysis project is descriptive response data without a verified tenant relationship to the access-token caller.
Project retrieval has inferred id but no verified tenant primary key or caller-project authorization mapping.
Account-event username identifies possible activity provenance rather than a verified event-owner authorization relation.
OAuth-client secret reset has account permissions but no caller-owner binding; public is a client attribute.
Curated podcast metadata lacks affirmative unrestricted-access evidence despite public-looking content.
Benefit-in-kind deletion has employer context but unknown security and wrapper-only response data.
Concept employee detail exposes personal information without any supplied caller authorization relationship.
Bundle-product option update has unknown security and no ownership or caller role evidence.
Guest-cart gift-card mutation is not inherently unrestricted; supplied fields lack cart authorization semantics.
Cart response mixes customer_id, company_id and creator_id without verified keys or a clear individual-versus-tenant policy.
Global auth-module adminUsername configures an upstream account rather than proving the API caller requires admin role.
Data-exporter tenant and teams fields are inferred location metadata, not a verified caller authorization relationship.
Starting automation emails requires Basic authentication but only generic result fields describe the response.
Address-key createdBy is provenance and read/write booleans do not establish the caller's ownership rule.
Blocking another account changes a caller relationship, not ownership of the target account, and no supported lookup is provided.
Follower visibility depends on account-owner settings, so bearer authentication and account ID do not imply public or owner-only access.
Summary limits lists to those the caller created, but lists lack an owner field and the path identifies another account.
Featuring an account on a public profile is an authenticated mutation, not unrestricted access to the target account.
Unfollowing an account changes a caller relationship and does not establish ownership of the target account object.
Annotation createdBy is scientific provenance rather than caller ownership; security remains unknown.
Gene lookup has scientific identifiers but no affirmative unrestricted API-access statement.
